articles.author: Rajguru Yadav
articles.description:
Hey Dev Community 👋

I'm Raj Guru Yadav, a 16-year-old full-stack web developer from India 🇮🇳

I've built 700+ projects (yes, really!) — but I still make mistakes. And this is the story of how one single line of JavaScript deleted my entire app’s data.
I was working on a small personal project — a student manager web app using just HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
Features included:
Add, Edit, Delete students

Store all data in localStorage

Beautiful dark UI with class cards



I had just finished the base version and added login functionality.

Everything looked great...
Until I wrote this line:
localStorage.clear(); // 🤦‍♂️

💥 The Disaster
Everything was gone.
All student records: deleted
All class data: deleted
All progress: vanished
Why?
🧠 What I Should Have Done Instead
function clearSessionData() {
  for (let key in localStorage) {
    if (key.startsWith("session_")) {
      localStorage.removeItem(key);
    }
  }
}

And always confirm with the user:
if (confirm("Are you sure you want to clear session data?")) {
  clearSessionData();
}


💾 I Also Added a Backup System
localStorage.setItem("backup_students", localStorage.getItem("students"));

This lets me restore in emergencies.
"Boss! Are you sure you want to delete all data?"
"Okay… I warned you." 😅
Sometimes, humor saves your app too.
🧘 What I Learned
Never assume clear() is harmless
Backups are life
Even mistakes make you better
🫂 Final Thought
Have YOU ever broken your own app?
🙌 Stay Connected
— Raj Guru Yadav
articles.title: I Lost All My App Data with One Line of Code — Here's What I Learned (Real JS Story)

articles.author: Max Will
articles.description:
Annotating regular images is hard enough but when you’re working with satellite or drone data, the challenges multiply. From variable lighting and altitude to inconsistent terrain and seasonal change, labeling these images requires a different set of rules entirely.
A solid satellite and drone image annotation workflow starts with understanding how spatial resolution and perspective affect label reliability. Is that bare soil or disease? A shadow or a road? The wrong annotation at this scale can derail downstream yield prediction models or environmental assessments.
For devs building geospatial AI systems, it's not just about drawing boxes — it’s about integrating multiple sensors, maintaining temporal consistency, and designing annotation pipelines that adapt to real-world edge cases. This article breaks down how agricultural use cases in Canada are pushing annotation workflows to handle weather variability, crop diversity, and regional farming practices.
As more vision models move outdoors and into the sky, labeling infrastructure needs to evolve — and developers building the pipelines need to be thinking at field scale, not pixel scale.
articles.title: How Satellite and Drone Image Annotation Powers Real-World AI

articles.author: Zen Oh
articles.description:
When you SSH into a server, sometimes you need to run a script that takes a long time to execute. You have to keep the connection open while the script is running—otherwise, it might fail (for example, if your internet connection gets disconnected).
tmux is a terminal multiplexer. It lets you switch easily between several programs in one terminal, detach them (so they keep running in the background), and reattach them later.
Here are the common commands I usually use with tmux:
tmux new -s s1

Ctrl + b then d
tmux ls

tmux attach -t s1

tmux kill-session -t s1
articles.title: tmux Cheatsheet
